title: Pool page layout
question: Kiln stays the look, standings lead, and scoring happens on the court. Pick how the pool page lays out its schedule, steer one, or re-roll.

options.label: Slot cards
options.lineage: the rotation cards a pool captain holds, one per round
options.thesis: Standings, then the schedule as a row of slot cards you swipe through, opening on the slot being played now.
options.viewport: Ink band with the pool name and its courts; the standings table with advancing places in amber; below, one wide slot card in view (Slot 3 · Now) with each court's match, score chips and a 'Score on Court 1' link, then who observes and rests; neighbouring slots peek at the edges.
options.risk: Only one slot is visible at a time, so reading the whole day means swiping.

regions.label: Slot 3 · Now: courts, scores, score on court

options.label: Team by team
options.lineage: a player asking 'when do we play next?'
options.thesis: Standings where each team's row opens to its own matches: results played, and the next one with slot and court.
options.viewport: Ink band; the standings table with a 'Next: Slot 3 · Court 2' line under each team, and tapping a team opens its results and remaining matches; a compact slot-by-slot list follows for the whole schedule.
options.risk: The schedule as a whole is secondary; an organizer scanning the day reads the compact list lower down.

options.label: Pool sheet
options.lineage: the printed round-robin sheet taped to the scorer's table
options.thesis: Standings, then the classic round-robin grid: every team against every other, each cell the result or when they play.
options.viewport: Ink band; standings; then a grid with teams down and across, each cell a score (winner's side in amber) or 'Slot 3 · Ct 1' for matches to come, the current slot's cells lit; the slot list with observing and resting follows.
options.risk: A grid of 5+ teams gets tight on a phone; it scrolls sideways inside its card there.
